1.title: A phone call about a delayed furniture delivery
1.script:
Maria: Hello, Northway Furniture, this is Maria speaking. How can I help you?
Daniel: Hi Maria. My name is Daniel Brooks. I ordered a sofa three weeks ago, and it was supposed to arrive last Friday. I'm still waiting.
Maria: Oh, I'm so sorry about that, Mr. Brooks. Let me check your order. Hmm, it looks like the sofa was delayed at our warehouse in Hamilton.
Daniel: That's frustrating. I took a day off work on Friday to be home for the delivery.
Maria: I completely understand. The good news is the truck leaves tomorrow morning, so you could have it by Thursday afternoon.
Daniel: Thursday is difficult. I'm working until six. Could it come on Saturday instead?
Maria: Let me see. Saturday has a morning slot between nine and noon. Would that work?
Daniel: That's perfect. And since I lost a day of work, is there any compensation?
Maria: Absolutely. I can take fifteen percent off the delivery fee, which brings it down to thirty-four dollars.
Daniel: Okay, that's fair. Thanks for your help, Maria.
Maria: My pleasure. You'll get a confirmation email within the hour.

questions.question: Why is Daniel calling the store?
options: He wants to cancel his order
His sofa has not been delivered
He wants to change the colour of his sofa
questions.explanation: Dice que el sofá debía llegar el viernes pasado y sigue esperando.

questions.question: What caused the delay?
questions.explanation: Maria menciona que se retrasó en el almacén de Hamilton.

questions.question: When will the sofa be delivered?
questions.explanation: Daniel no puede el jueves y acuerdan el sábado entre nueve y mediodía.

questions.question: What does Maria offer Daniel?
options: A discount on the delivery fee
questions.explanation: Ofrece quince por ciento de descuento en el costo de entrega.

1.title: A call to reschedule a dentist appointment
1.script:
Tom: Good morning, Bayview Dental. Tom speaking.
Priya: Hi Tom, it's Priya Shah. I have a cleaning appointment tomorrow at ten, but something came up and I need to move it.
Tom: No problem, Priya. Let me look at the calendar. What day were you thinking?
Priya: I'm free on Wednesday or Friday, but only in the afternoon. My daughter has a school play in the morning on Friday.
Tom: Wednesday afternoon is completely booked, I'm afraid. We have a spot on Friday at two thirty with Doctor Nguyen.
Priya: Doctor Nguyen? I usually see Doctor Patel.
Tom: Doctor Patel is on vacation until the end of the month. But Doctor Nguyen is excellent, and she has the same cleaning procedure.
Priya: Well, I'd rather wait for Doctor Patel, to be honest. Is there anything in the first week of next month?
Tom: Let me check. Yes, Tuesday the third at four o'clock.
Priya: Perfect, I'll take that one. Do I need to bring anything?
Tom: Just your insurance card. And please arrive ten minutes early to fill out a new form.

questions.question: Why does Priya call the dental office?
questions.explanation: Quiere mover su cita de limpieza de mañana.

questions.question: Why can't Priya come on Friday morning?
options: Her daughter has a school event
Her car is at the garage
questions.explanation: Su hija tiene una obra escolar el viernes por la mañana.

questions.question: Why does Priya refuse the Friday appointment?
questions.explanation: Prefiere esperar a la doctora Patel, que es su dentista habitual.

questions.question: What will Priya do on the day of her visit?
options: Arrive early to complete a form
questions.explanation: Tom le pide llegar diez minutos antes para llenar un formulario.

1.title: A call to a landlord about a broken heater
1.script:
Mr. Lee: Hello, Lee Property Management.
Karen: Hi, Mr. Lee, it's Karen from apartment twelve. The heater in my living room stopped working two days ago, and it's getting really cold at night.
Mr. Lee: Oh no, I'm sorry to hear that. Did you check if the thermostat has fresh batteries?
Karen: Yes, I replaced them yesterday. The display works, but the heater doesn't turn on.
Mr. Lee: Okay. Then it's probably the valve. I'll send our technician, Raj. He's available tomorrow afternoon, around three. Would you be home?
Karen: I work until five, but my neighbour Mrs. Alvarez has a spare key. I can ask her to let him in.
Mr. Lee: That works. In the meantime, I can drop off a small electric heater this evening if you want.
Karen: That would be wonderful. I'd really appreciate it.
Mr. Lee: I'll bring it by around seven. Please remember to keep it away from the curtains.
Karen: Of course. Thank you so much for the quick response.

questions.question: What is Karen's problem?
options: Her living room heater does not work
questions.explanation: El calefactor de la sala dejó de funcionar hace dos días.

questions.question: What does Karen say she already did?
questions.explanation: Dice que cambió las pilas ayer.

questions.question: How will the technician get into the apartment?
options: Karen will leave early from work
Mr. Lee will open the door
Mrs. Alvarez will let him in
questions.explanation: Karen le pedirá a su vecina, que tiene una llave de repuesto.

questions.question: What will Mr. Lee do this evening?
questions.explanation: Ofrece dejar un calefactor eléctrico pequeño alrededor de las siete.

2.title: Two neighbours chatting about a garden
2.script:
Emma: Hey Carlos! Your tomatoes look amazing this year. What's your secret?
Carlos: Honestly, Emma, it's just lots of sun and a bit of compost. My dad taught me years ago.
Emma: I tried growing tomatoes last summer, but the leaves turned yellow and I lost most of them.
Carlos: Yellow leaves usually mean too much water. You know, I only water mine twice a week, early in the morning.
Emma: Oh, I was watering every single day. That explains it!
Carlos: Don't feel bad, everybody does that at the beginning. Hey, I have way too many tomatoes. Would you like a few?
Emma: Oh, that's so kind. I could make a pasta sauce tonight.
Carlos: Great idea. Come by on Saturday, and I'll give you some seedlings for next year too.
Emma: Deal. I'll bring cookies. I just baked a batch with chocolate and oatmeal.
Carlos: Now you're talking. See you Saturday.

questions.question: What do the neighbours mainly talk about?
questions.explanation: Hablan de los tomates de Carlos y los de Emma.

questions.question: According to Carlos, what likely went wrong with Emma's plants?
questions.explanation: Las hojas amarillas suelen indicar exceso de agua.

questions.question: What will Emma probably do with the tomatoes?
questions.explanation: Dice que podría hacer una salsa de pasta esta noche.

questions.question: What will Emma bring on Saturday?
questions.explanation: Promete llevar galletas de chocolate y avena.

2.title: Coworkers deciding where to have lunch
2.script:
Jamal: Hey Sofia, are you free for lunch? I'm starving, and I've been in meetings since eight.
Sofia: Definitely. Where do you feel like going? The sandwich place is closed for renovations.
Jamal: Oh, that's a shame. What about the new Thai restaurant on King Street?
Sofia: I heard it's good, but a little pricey. Last week Mark said his lunch cost nearly twenty-five dollars.
Jamal: Hmm, that's too much for a Wednesday. There's the food truck near the park. They have great tacos for ten bucks.
Sofia: Love that idea, and it's sunny today. We can eat outside.
Jamal: Perfect. Should we invite Mark and Linda?
Sofia: Linda is on a deadline, so she'll skip lunch. I'll text Mark though.
Jamal: Sounds good. Let's leave at twelve fifteen so we beat the line.
Sofia: Great. I'll grab my jacket and meet you at the elevator.

questions.question: Why can't they eat at the sandwich place?
questions.explanation: Sofia dice que está cerrado por renovaciones.

questions.question: Why do they reject the Thai restaurant?
questions.explanation: Mark pagó casi veinticinco dólares; les parece demasiado.

questions.question: Where will they eat?
questions.explanation: Eligen el camión de comida cerca del parque.

questions.question: Why won't Linda join them?
questions.explanation: Linda tiene una fecha límite.

2.title: Friends planning a weekend hike
2.script:
Olivia: Ben, did you check the weather for Saturday? I really want to do the lake trail.
Ben: I did, and it's looking good. Sunny in the morning, but there's a chance of rain after three o'clock.
Olivia: Then let's start early. How about meeting at seven thirty?
Ben: Seven thirty on a Saturday? You're kidding, right? Can we say eight?
Olivia: Fine, eight. The trail takes about four hours, so we'd be done around noon.
Ben: Sounds perfect. Should I bring lunch for both of us?
Olivia: Don't worry, I'll pack sandwiches. You could bring the snacks and the water bottles.
Ben: Deal. Oh, and my cousin Mia wants to come too. Is that okay?
Olivia: Of course! The more the merrier. Just tell her to wear proper hiking boots. Last time the path was really muddy.
Ben: I'll let her know. See you at eight at the parking lot.

questions.question: What is the weather forecast for Saturday?
options: Sunny with rain in the afternoon
questions.explanation: Sol por la mañana y posibilidad de lluvia después de las tres.

questions.question: What time will they meet?
questions.explanation: Ben negocia y acuerdan las ocho.

questions.question: What will Ben bring?
questions.explanation: Olivia lleva los sándwiches; Ben lleva bocadillos y agua.

questions.question: What does Olivia ask Ben to tell Mia?
questions.explanation: Debe usar botas adecuadas porque el sendero estaba muy fangoso.

3.title: Information about a community recycling program
3.script:
Victor: Hi, I'm calling about the new recycling program in the city. I have a few questions.
Hannah: Of course. I'm happy to explain. Starting next month, every home will get a blue bin for paper and plastic, and a green bin for food waste.
Victor: Do I need to pay for the bins?
Hannah: No, they're free. You can pick them up at the community centre on Elm Street from the first of the month. Just bring a piece of identification with your address.
Victor: And how often is the collection?
Hannah: The blue bin is collected every second Tuesday, and the green bin every Thursday, because food waste smells in the summer.
Victor: What happens if I put the wrong item in the bin?
Hannah: The collectors will leave a yellow tag explaining the mistake, and they won't take the bin that week. After three warnings, there is a fifty-dollar fine.
Victor: I see. Is there a guide so I know what goes where?
Hannah: Yes, there's an online guide, and we'll also mail a magnet with the main rules to every address.

questions.question: What will each home receive?
questions.explanation: Un contenedor azul y uno verde.

questions.question: What does Victor need to pick up his bins?
questions.explanation: Debe llevar una identificación con su dirección.

questions.question: Why is the green bin collected more often?
questions.explanation: Hannah explica que los desechos de comida huelen en verano.

questions.question: What happens after three warnings?
questions.explanation: Hay una multa de cincuenta dólares.

3.title: Information about a library membership
3.script:
Noah: Hello, I just moved to the area and I'd like to know how to get a library card.
Grace: Welcome to the neighbourhood! Getting a card is easy and free. You just need a photo ID and a document that shows your new address, like a utility bill.
Noah: Can I borrow both books and movies?
Grace: Yes, you can borrow up to fifteen items at a time. Books are for three weeks, and movies for one week.
Noah: What if I forget to return something on time?
Grace: There are no late fees for books anymore, but movies have a fine of fifty cents per day.
Noah: That's reasonable. I also work from home. Do you have quiet spaces?
Grace: We have study rooms on the second floor. You can reserve one for up to two hours through our website. They have free wifi and power outlets.
Noah: Excellent. And are there any programs for kids? I have a six-year-old.
Grace: Every Saturday at ten, we have a story hour. It's very popular, so I'd suggest coming early.

questions.question: What does Noah need to get a card?
options: Photo ID and proof of address
questions.explanation: Necesita identificación con foto y un comprobante de domicilio.

questions.question: How long can Noah keep a movie?
questions.explanation: Las películas se prestan por una semana.

questions.question: What is the penalty for late movies?
questions.explanation: Cincuenta centavos por día.

questions.question: What does Grace recommend for the story hour?
questions.explanation: Es muy popular, por eso sugiere llegar temprano.

3.title: Information about a bus pass
3.script:
Peter: Hi, I'm a new student at the university, and I'd like to know about monthly bus passes.
Leila: Sure! Students get a discounted pass. It costs seventy-two dollars a month, instead of the regular one hundred and twenty.
Peter: That's a big difference. How do I get it?
Leila: You need to show your student card at the transit office downtown, and we'll load the pass onto a transit card. The card itself costs six dollars.
Peter: Does the pass work on the subway as well?
Leila: Yes, it covers all buses, streetcars, and the subway in the city, but not the airport train.
Peter: Good to know. Can I get a refund if I lose the card?
Leila: If you register the card online, we can transfer the balance to a new one. If it's not registered, unfortunately, we can't.
Peter: I'll definitely register it, then. What are the office hours?
Leila: Monday to Friday, eight to six. On Saturdays, we close at noon.

questions.question: How much is the student monthly pass?
questions.explanation: Cuesta setenta y dos dólares al mes.

questions.question: What does Peter need to bring to the office?
questions.explanation: Debe mostrar su credencial de estudiante.

questions.question: What is NOT covered by the pass?
questions.explanation: Cubre todo excepto el tren al aeropuerto.

questions.question: What should Peter do to protect his balance?
questions.explanation: Si registra la tarjeta, pueden transferir el saldo.

4.title: Local news: a new bridge and a street festival
4.script:
Announcer: Good morning, and welcome to your local news update. Our top story: the city has announced that the old Riverside Bridge will close for repairs starting Monday, and it will stay closed for about six months. Drivers are asked to use the Maple Avenue Bridge instead, and extra buses will run along that route during rush hour. The mayor says the work is necessary because engineers found cracks in the support beams last spring.
In lighter news, the annual Harvest Street Festival returns this weekend in the downtown core. More than eighty vendors will sell food, crafts, and local art. Live music begins at noon on Saturday, and a children's parade will start at two o'clock. Organizers expect around ten thousand visitors, so parking will be limited. They encourage everyone to take public transit or ride a bike. Admission is free, but donations will support the local food bank. That's all for now. Stay tuned for the weather.

questions.question: What will happen to the Riverside Bridge?
options: It will open to bicycles only
questions.explanation: Cerrará por reparaciones durante unos seis meses.

questions.question: Why is the work necessary?
options: Because of cracks in the beams
questions.explanation: Los ingenieros encontraron grietas en las vigas de soporte.

questions.question: When does the children's parade begin?
questions.explanation: El desfile infantil empieza a las dos.

questions.question: What are visitors encouraged to do?
questions.explanation: El estacionamiento será limitado.

4.title: Local news: a library reopening and a weather alert
4.script:
Announcer: Good evening. In today's headlines, the Central Library will reopen on Thursday after a year of renovations. The new building features a rooftop reading garden, a recording studio for teenagers, and twice as many computers as before. The library board says the project cost twelve million dollars, and most of the money came from provincial funding. The grand opening ceremony begins at ten in the morning, and the first one hundred visitors will receive a free tote bag.
Meanwhile, Environment Canada has issued a freezing rain warning for tomorrow night. Temperatures are expected to drop below zero after eight o'clock, which could make roads and sidewalks very slippery. Drivers should reduce their speed, and residents are advised to keep an emergency kit at home. Several school boards say they will decide early tomorrow whether classes will be cancelled on Friday. We'll keep you updated throughout the night.

questions.question: When will the Central Library reopen?
questions.explanation: Reabre el jueves.

questions.question: Which feature is new in the library?
questions.explanation: Tiene un jardín de lectura en la azotea y un estudio de grabación.

questions.question: Who will receive a free tote bag?
questions.explanation: Los primeros cien visitantes.

questions.question: What are drivers advised to do during the freezing rain?
questions.explanation: Se recomienda reducir la velocidad.

4.title: Local news: a new bike lane and a job fair
4.script:
Announcer: Welcome to the midday news. City council voted last night to build a protected bike lane along Queen Street. Construction will begin in April and should finish by September. The lane will remove about forty parking spaces, which some business owners oppose, but supporters say it will make the street safer for cyclists and attract more customers. A public meeting will take place on March fifth at city hall, where residents can share their opinions.
And if you are looking for work, the Spring Job Fair takes place next Wednesday at the convention centre. More than one hundred employers will attend, including hospitals, banks, and technology companies. The event runs from nine to four, and admission is free. Organizers recommend bringing several copies of your resume and dressing professionally. Free workshops on interview skills will be offered every hour in Room B. Now, let's check the traffic.

questions.question: What did the city council vote to build?
questions.explanation: Aprobaron un carril bici protegido en Queen Street.

questions.question: Why do some business owners oppose the project?
questions.explanation: Eliminará unos cuarenta espacios de estacionamiento.

questions.question: Where will the Spring Job Fair take place?
questions.explanation: Será en el centro de convenciones.

questions.question: What are job seekers advised to bring?
questions.explanation: Recomiendan llevar varias copias del currículum.

5.title: Three colleagues discussing a team retreat
5.script:
Rachel: Okay everyone, we need to decide where to hold our team retreat this fall. I have two ideas: a lodge in the mountains, or a day at the city's escape rooms and a nice dinner.
Amir: I vote for the mountains. We spend all year in front of screens, and being in nature would help us relax and bond. The lodge is a two-hour drive, but it's worth it.
Julie: I'm not so sure, Amir. The lodge costs about four hundred dollars per person, with the overnight stay. The city option is only eighty dollars, and nobody has to take time away from their families.
Amir: True, but the point of a retreat is to disconnect, and a dinner downtown doesn't feel very different from a normal evening.
Rachel: Julie has a good point about the budget, though. We only have eight thousand dollars for the whole team of twenty.
Julie: Exactly. With the city option we could even afford a workshop with a facilitator.
Amir: Okay, a facilitator is a nice benefit. Maybe we could do a shorter, one-night mountain trip?
Rachel: Hmm, that might be a compromise. Let me check prices and send both options by email.

questions.question: What is the discussion about?
questions.explanation: Deciden dónde hacer el retiro del equipo.

questions.question: Why does Amir prefer the mountains?
options: Nature would help the team relax
questions.explanation: Cree que la naturaleza ayudaría a relajarse y conectar.

questions.question: What is Julie's main concern?
questions.explanation: El albergue cuesta cuatrocientos dólares por persona.

questions.question: What does Rachel decide to do?
options: Check prices and email both options
questions.explanation: Revisará precios y enviará ambas opciones por correo.

5.title: Three roommates deciding about a pet
5.script:
Chloe: So, guys, I've been thinking that we should adopt a cat. The apartment feels a little empty, and I'd love some company when I study.
Marcus: A cat? I'm allergic, Chloe. Last time I visited my aunt, I couldn't stop sneezing. Maybe a fish tank instead?
Nina: A fish tank is boring, Marcus. But honestly, I'm worried about the cost. Vet bills can be really high, and the landlord asks for a two hundred dollar pet deposit.
Chloe: I can pay the deposit. I'd also take care of the food and the litter box.
Nina: That's generous, but who will look after the cat when you go home for the holidays?
Chloe: Hmm, I hadn't thought about that. Maybe a neighbour could help.
Marcus: What if we try fostering one for a month first? The shelter offers that, and it's free. Then we'd see if my allergies are manageable.
Nina: I like that idea. It's less of a commitment.
Chloe: Fine, I'm willing to try a foster cat first. I'll call the shelter tomorrow.

questions.question: What does Chloe want?
questions.explanation: Quiere adoptar un gato.

questions.question: Why is Marcus against the idea?
questions.explanation: Es alérgico a los gatos.

questions.question: What worries Nina?
questions.explanation: Le preocupan las cuentas del veterinario y el depósito.

questions.question: What is the final decision?
questions.explanation: Probarán cuidando un gato temporalmente en el refugio.

5.title: Three neighbours discussing a community garden
5.script:
Fatima: Thanks for coming, everyone. The city is offering us the empty lot behind the parking area for a community garden. We have to decide if we want to apply.
George: I think it's a wonderful idea. Fresh vegetables, and a place to meet our neighbours. I'd be happy to build the raised beds myself.
Helen: I like the idea too, George, but who will maintain it? Gardens need watering every day, and many of us are busy.
Fatima: We could create a schedule, with two families per week.
Helen: That could work, but what about the cost? Soil and seeds aren't free.
George: The city covers the first year of soil, and a local nursery offered us a discount on plants.
Helen: Oh, I didn't know that. In that case, I'm in favour. But I still think we need rules, so people don't take vegetables that aren't theirs.
Fatima: Absolutely. I'll write a draft of the rules and bring it to the next meeting on the twelfth.
George: Perfect. I'll start sketching a layout in the meantime.

questions.question: What is the city offering?
questions.explanation: Ofrece el terreno baldío detrás del estacionamiento.

questions.question: What is Helen's first concern?
questions.explanation: Pregunta quién se encargará del riego diario.

questions.question: What changes Helen's opinion?
questions.explanation: Se entera de que la ciudad cubre la tierra y hay descuentos.

questions.question: What will Fatima do next?
options: Write a draft of the rules
questions.explanation: Escribirá un borrador de reglas para la reunión del doce.

6.title: A report on a proposed four-day work week
6.script: Reporter: A proposal to move the city's municipal employees to a four-day work week is dividing opinion at city hall. Councillor Patel supports the idea. She says similar programs in other countries improved morale and reduced sick days, and she believes it would help the city attract younger workers. However, Mr. Johnson, who leads the taxpayers' association, is against it. He argues that residents expect services five days a week, and he worries that longer shifts could lead to mistakes. The union representative, Ms. Tran, welcomes the pilot project, but she wants employees to have a say in which day they take off. Finally, the city manager, Mr. Wilson, is neutral for now. He says he would like to see a six-month trial and a detailed report on costs before making a recommendation. A vote is scheduled for the end of next month.

questions.question: Who supports the four-day work week without conditions?
questions.explanation: La concejal Patel lo apoya porque mejora la moral y reduce ausencias.

questions.question: Why is Mr. Johnson against it?
questions.explanation: Cree que los residentes esperan servicio cinco días y teme errores.

questions.question: What does Ms. Tran want?
options: A say in the day off
questions.explanation: Quiere que los empleados opinen sobre qué día libran.

questions.question: What is Mr. Wilson's position?
questions.explanation: Es neutral y pide una prueba de seis meses y un informe de costos.

6.title: A report on a new electric bus program
6.script: Reporter: The regional transit authority wants to replace its diesel buses with electric ones over the next ten years, and local reaction is mixed. Mayor Alvarez strongly supports the plan. He says electric buses will cut pollution in the downtown core and reduce long-term fuel costs. Dr. Kim, an environmental scientist, agrees, but she warns that the electricity must come from clean sources, otherwise the benefits will be limited. On the other side, Mr. Roberts, the head of the drivers' association, is concerned that the new buses have a shorter range, which could force routes to be shortened in winter. He also points out that each electric bus costs nearly twice as much as a diesel one. Meanwhile, rider advocate Ms. Singh is cautiously optimistic. She likes the quieter ride, but she insists that fares must not increase to pay for the change.

questions.question: Why does Mayor Alvarez support the plan?
options: It will reduce pollution and fuel costs
questions.explanation: Dice que reducirá la contaminación y los costos de combustible.

questions.question: What condition does Dr. Kim mention?
questions.explanation: La electricidad debe provenir de fuentes limpias.

questions.question: What worries Mr. Roberts?
questions.explanation: Teme que el menor alcance obligue a acortar rutas en invierno.

questions.question: What does Ms. Singh insist on?
questions.explanation: Exige que las tarifas no suban.

6.title: A report on a proposal to extend library hours
6.script: Reporter: A proposal to keep the public library open until midnight on weekdays has sparked a lively debate. Student leader Diego Ruiz is strongly in favour. He says many students have no quiet place to study at night, and the extra hours would help them prepare for exams. Library director Ms. O'Connor also supports the idea, but she says she would need to hire at least six more staff members, which would cost about two hundred thousand dollars a year. Councillor Bennett, however, is not convinced. He believes the money should be used to fix local roads, and he suggests opening only on Fridays as a test. Finally, local resident Mrs. Grant is concerned about safety. She doesn't want people walking home alone late at night, and she asks the city to improve street lighting before approving the change.

questions.question: Why does Diego Ruiz support the proposal?
options: Students need quiet places to study
questions.explanation: Muchos estudiantes no tienen lugar tranquilo para estudiar de noche.

questions.question: What does Ms. O'Connor say the library would need?
questions.explanation: Necesitaría contratar al menos seis empleados más.

questions.question: What does Councillor Bennett suggest?
options: Opening only on Fridays as a test
questions.explanation: Prefiere reparar calles y propone probar solo los viernes.

questions.question: What does Mrs. Grant ask for?
questions.explanation: Pide mejorar el alumbrado antes de aprobar el cambio.
